extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, geometers, and historians of mathematics (advanced students and researchers interested in classical geometric constructions)
extracted.subtask_description: Constructing (and analysing) polygons (triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, n‑gons) inscribed in a given circle whose sides are required to pass through given points or be parallel to given lines; includes case enumeration, lemmas, and demonstrations in the classical (ancient) geometric style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis versus construction (what counts as a solution)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the ancient geometry tradition a problem was often considered solved when the analysis had been effected; many continental writers likewise 'contented themselves with giving merely the analysis of the problem.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete treatment should supply both the analysis (reduction/idea) and a geometrical construction with a demonstration (the common modern/ancient expectation differs). If only analysis is given, state explicitly that a construction/demonstration is missing and whether the author or tradition accepts analysis alone as a solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumeration of relative cases (completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different relative positions of the given points with respect to the circle (inside/outside, on the circle) and to each other produce multiple distinct cases that require modifications in analysis and composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and treat all positional cases (e.g., one point inside and another outside yields two distinct triangles; AB passing through the centre is a special case, etc.). Explicitly indicate how the construction changes per case and whether multiple solutions arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination and indetermination (existence/uniqueness/degeneracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify when the problem is determinate, indeterminate, or impossible, and state which additional determinations are necessary under given circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse and record determinations (parameters that must be fixed) and indeterminate configurations; e.g., Lhuilier and others are criticized for incomplete treatment of determinations and indeterminate cases. Note when a case is 'inevitably impossible or indeterminate.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Odd versus even number of sides (structural distinction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The method differs fundamentally for odd‑sided and even‑sided polygons: for odd‑sided polygons the determining line touches a determinable circle, while for even‑sided polygons the corresponding line is parallel to a determinable line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When generalising methods to n‑gons, explicitly separate the odd and even cases and adapt the final determination step accordingly; this difference recurs and must be handled to extend constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to and explicit statement of lemmas
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems are reduced to simpler lemmas (for example: 'Through two given points to draw lines meeting in the circumference so that the line joining the other intersections with the circle shall be parallel to a given line').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and prove necessary lemmas up front (e.g., Lemma I and II for odd/even polygons) and show how the main construction reduces to these lemmas. Make lemmas explicit to structure the solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of purely geometrical (synthetic) method versus analytic/trigonometrical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference is expressed for strictly geometrical constructions (the ancient geometric method) and criticism is made when algebraic/trigonometrical/fractional forms are used where synthetic constructions are expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming a 'geometrical' solution, ensure it avoids non‑synthetic algebraic forms or clearly indicate when analytic steps are used; note historical criticisms (e.g., Euler's terms involving three factors or fractional forms not admissible in strict ancient geometry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful reversal of analysis to form demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The demonstration should generally consist of a reversal of the analysis; loci meeting at a point often require ex absurdo (reductio) methods, and steps must be checked for oversights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After producing an analysis and construction, present a formal demonstration by reversing the analysis and explicitly address any ex absurdo steps and minor oversights (as noted in Castillon's demonstration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic, stepwise construction using parallels/chords/tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive procedures are to be given as stepwise instructions: join given points, draw chords parallel to given lines, draw tangents, form secants, and iterate to obtain successive vertices (examples shown for triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, n‑gon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear sequence of construction steps (join AB, draw chord MN parallel to AB, from N draw NOP, etc.). For each step indicate the geometric reason (equal angles, rectangles equal to tangent squares, etc.) so the reader can follow/reverse the construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and justification of metric equalities (tangents, rectangles, products)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many constructions rely on metric relations (e.g., 'AB·AK = AF² = AO² − OF²', 'the rectangle AK·HB equals the square of KC or CH'), which must be established and used to identify given points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When invoking algebraic/metric equalities, show derivation or reference classical results (tangent‑square properties, equal rectangles) so the point(s) whose position/magnitude are asserted to be 'given' are indeed constructible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit accounting of intermediate constructibility (given in position and magnitude)
rubrics_metrics.description: At each key intermediate step show that constructed points/segments are 'given' in position and/or magnitude (e.g., from NK:KM being given infer NQ:QM is given and hence point Q is given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace constructibility of intermediate elements: if a ratio or chord length is shown to be given, explicitly conclude which points or chords are determinable, and how they lead to final vertices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt modern tools (poles/polars, transversals, coordinates) where advantageous
rubrics_metrics.description: The later continental development emphasised poles and polars (Brianchon, Gergonne, Annales) which unify properties of conics and provide powerful methods for these construction problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dealing with conics or general second‑order curves, consider recasting parts of the argument using poles/polars or coordinate/transversal methods to combine scattered properties into a uniform theory and simplify proofs.
